geo:GSE339010.title: Ultrasound-Mediated BBB Opening Promotes Microglial Reprogramming and Enhanced Endothelial Interactions in the Human Peritumoral Brain [scRNA-Seq]
geo:GSE339010.study_title: Ultrasound-Mediated BBB Opening Promotes Microglial Reprogramming and Enhanced Endothelial Interactions in the Human Peritumoral Brain [scRNA-Seq]
geo:GSE339010.notes: resp_score=0; gdstype=Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing
geo:GSE339010.description: The blood–brain barrier (BBB) restricts entry of therapeutics and shapes immune surveillance in the central nervous system, while microglia maintain barrier integrity and coordinate repair. Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound with intravenously administered microbubbles (LIPU/MB) transiently opens the BBB in patients, with restoration mostly occurring within about an hour; however, how microglia respond to LIPU/MB during this acute repair window in the human brain remains unknown. We report on intraoperative LIPU/MB studies where the peritumoral brain of glioblastoma patients was biopsied 45 minutes after sonication and analyzed, as part of phase I/II clinical trials (NCT04528680). We integrated single-cell RNA-seq, single-cell ATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and multiplex immunofluorescence. We observe that LIPU/MB modulates perivascular microglia by promoting extension of processes toward the endothelium, inducing pro-inflammatory and chemoattractant transcriptional programs, and remodeling of endothelial–myeloid ligand–receptor communication. We find that microglial reprogramming is accompanied by coordinated changes in chromatin accessibility and heightened activity of the AP-1 transcription factor complex. These results reveal that LIPU/MB-based BBB opening in humans does not merely permit drug passage but reprograms resident myeloid cells to engage the vasculature and amplify innate and adaptive immune pathways, providing a mechanistic basis to leverage immune activation by LIPU/MB with immunotherapies for brain tumors. These findings also warrant consideration in the context of the pathophysiology and therapeutics of CNS diseases where there is acute BBB disruption, or where LIPU/MB is under investigation.

geo:GSE342830.study_title: Ligand-based directed differentiation to produce granulosa-like cells expressing steroidogenic enzyme genes
geo:GSE342830.notes: resp_score=0; gdstype=Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing
geo:GSE342830.description: The ovarian granulosa cells are responsible for producing hormones and supporting oocytes through maturation and meiotic resumption. There is a need to generate granulosa-like cells (GLCs) from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) to better model human gonadal development and to test the effects of exogenous or pharmaceutical compounds on the ovary. Here we report a rapid ligand-based protocol for differentiating hiPSCs into cells that express markers of the transient developmental lineages and steroidogenic pathway genes. Single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis identified canonical granulosa cell genes were expressed in a subset of cells and identified new genes of interest that were significantly associated with computationally modeled pseudotime. HSD17B1 was expressed in resulting GLCs but at low levels, suggesting an immature granulosa cell phenotype. The GLCs were produced using a simple culture method that could be augmented for granulosa cell functions such as sustaining oocyte growth. Producing GLCs through protocols such as this one is a first step toward designing large-scale ovarian endocrinology assays and developing personalized cell-based fertility and hormone restoration technologies in the future.

geo:GSE343070.title: Landscape of the Tumor Microenvironment and Cellular Mechanisms in Pancreatic Cancer During Cachexia Progression
geo:GSE343070.study_title: Landscape of the Tumor Microenvironment and Cellular Mechanisms in Pancreatic Cancer During Cachexia Progression
geo:GSE343070.description: Cancer progression is associated with dynamic crosstalk between malignant cells and the tumor microenvironment (TME). However, the spatiotemporal mechanisms of the TME during cachexia progression remain poorly understood. Therefore, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and bulk transcriptomic analyses to reveal the molecular trajectories across the non-cachexia (non-CAC), pre-cachexia (Pre-CAC), and cachexia (CAC) stages. We identified a progressively expanding SEMA4A+ tumor subcluster with pro-inflammatory properties that directly induces muscle atrophy via SEMA4A, whose expression gradually increases during cachexia progression in PC patients. Importantly, SEMA4A+ tumor cells reprogram TME through polarizing macrophages towards an AQP9+ phenotype. In turn, these AQP9+ macrophages drive cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) into LOXL2+ CAFs. LOXL2+ CAFs subsequently facilitate FOSL1 and SEMA4A expression in tumor cells, establishing a self-reinforcing signaling circuit that promote PC cachexia. This cascade culminates in the formation of a triadic niche that drives cachexia progression in PC.

geo:GSE343367.study_title: JAX scRNAseq Study01- Single-cell RNA sequencing of male KOLF2.2J hiPSC-derived cortical brain organoids homozygous null for PAX6
geo:GSE343367.notes: resp_score=0; gdstype=Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing
geo:GSE343367.description: This study characterizes the transcriptional dynamics underlying cortical brain organoid development in the absence of the transcription factor PAX6. A PAX6 null allele was engineered by introducing a premature termination codon causing a frameshift mutation (PTC+1). Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed on samples collected at days 7, 8, and 9 following the initiation of differentiation from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs), enabling a detailed temporal analysis of gene expression changes.
